No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result WTC Abuja Uses Sports To Boost Workers’ Productivity by Bidon Mibzar 17 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The World Trade Centre (WTC), Abuja, has introduced a sporting initiative to promote workplace wellness, improve productivity and strengthen business relationships among companies and professionals operating within its commercial community.
The initiative, launched through the maiden Chairman’s Cup Tennis Tournament featuring lawn tennis and table tennis competitions, is designed to encourage healthier lifestyles and create opportunities for business operators to interact beyond their usual office engagements.
The competition, launched on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, also reflects growing recognition of the importance of physical and mental well-being in sustaining workplace productivity.
Speaking on the initiative, the Vice President of WTC Abuja, Mr Ahmed Karim, said the tournament was conceived to build a community where occupants could develop relationships, promote healthy living and support one another beyond occupying office spaces.
Karim explained that the Centre had recently attracted business occupants interested in building a community, fostering friendships and improving the welfare of people working within its premises.
He said the tournament would allow tenants to interact, understand one another’s businesses and establish relationships that could translate into meaningful commercial partnerships.
According to him, a successful business environment should be measured not only by the quality of its infrastructure and office facilities but also by the well-being and relationships of the people who operate within it.
Karim noted that sports remained a unifying force across societies, bringing together people from different ethnic, cultural and professional backgrounds while promoting healthy competition and cooperation.
He added that the Chairman’s Cup could expand beyond tennis and table tennis, disclosing that the Centre was considering introducing five-a-side football competitions and developing two paddle courts to provide additional recreational opportunities.
The WTC vice president said winners of the maiden competition would receive prizes, including the Chairman’s Cup for the overall winner.
He expressed optimism that subsequent editions would attract wider participation and incorporate more sporting activities.
Also underscoring the importance of the initiative, Roberto Pozzi, who represented the Managing Director of Nigeria Agip Exploration (NAE), Maurizio Pinna, said recreational activities were necessary for professionals working in demanding corporate environments.
Pozzi, whose company operates from the World Trade Centre, said sporting activities would promote teamwork, encourage collaboration and provide workers with a healthy break from their regular responsibilities.
He explained that sports helped professionals manage workplace stress, clear their minds and regain the mental alertness required to make sound decisions.
According to him, physical exercise also improves reaction time, decision-making and mental performance, making recreational activities particularly important for workers dealing with heavy workloads and demanding corporate targets.
The initiative is anchored on WTC Abuja’s ‘Live, Play, Work’ philosophy, which seeks to integrate business activities with recreation, wellness and community engagement rather than restrict the Centre’s environment to conventional office operations.
The Chairman’s Cup is expected to serve as a platform for building professional networks, encouraging healthy lifestyles and strengthening the sense of community among businesses operating within the World Trade Centre, Abuja.
